sentences: Adding two services to its Financial Services Data platform, Oracle has announced the launch of Oracle Financial Services Data Intelligence Treasury Analytics and Oracle Financial Services Data Intelligence Customer Analytics.
The two analytics applications will give AI-assisted exploration into curated finserv data to help financial institutions analyse data and inform business strategy.
Jason Wynne , Senior Vice President of Product Management at Oracle Financial Services says: “Financial institutions don’t need more dashboards: they need faster answers they can trust.
Disconnected reports, manual analysis and inconsistent data definitions can make timely analysis more difficult.
The two applications aim to provide a unified, AI-assisted analytical foundation.
Business leaders can use it to examine trends and identify what is driving changes in performance.

“Together, these applications establish a foundation for continued AI innovation across Oracle Financial Services, with the goal of making insights more accessible and relevant to financial services teams,” Jason adds.

Oracle Financial Services Data Intelligence Treasury Analytics helps treasury, finance and risk leaders gain a connected view of liquidity, funding, cash flow, balance sheet performance and market risk.
Using natural-language questions and automatically generated insights, teams can explore liquidity and funding trends and investigate unusual patterns.
They can also identify what contributes to changes in balance sheet performance.
Oracle’s product information says the application brings together interest rate sensitivity, asset liability management (ALM), funds transfer pricing (FTP) and margin perspectives.
Through this, Oracle aims to help inform the funding and liquidity decisions of financial advisors and insurers.

Together, these applications establish a foundation for continued AI innovation across Oracle Financial Services, with the goal of making insights more accessible and relevant to financial services teams
Oracle Financial Services Data Intelligence Customer Analytics helps financial institutions understand customer profitability, product adoption, portfolio performance and retention opportunities.

Bringing together customer, product, channel, geography, lifecycle and profitability data in a single analytical experience, the solution then uses AI-assisted exploration to helps businesses examine changes in customer behaviour to investigate growth and retention opportunities.
It is this unified data foundation which can reduce the need to manually reconcile information across customer, ledger, profitability and cost management, treasury and risk systems.
Oracle’s documentation lists prebuilt use cases including customer profitability analysis, relationship manager performance monitoring and dormant-to-active customer re-engagement analytics.
On top of AI-assisted exploration, Oracle’s AI Assistant lets business users ask questions in natural language and generate visualisations without building reports manually.
Auto Insights automatically discovers patterns in the underlying data.
Oracle says AI-assisted exploration helps users move from what happened to why it happened and where further analysis or action may be needed.
What is more, a shared analytics model and semantic layer provide consistent financial services definitions, which Oracle positions as the basis for business use of the AI tools.
The curated data foundation acts as a base for future agentic AI applications across its financial services portfolio.

Deloitte partners with Oracle to implement its financial services applications for banks, and a 2025 solution brief sets out joint work across finance transformation, core banking and regulatory reporting.
In 2024 it worked with FPT and Oracle to complete the anti-money laundering and fraud risk components at MB Bank.
The alliance gives Oracle an implementation partner for OFSAA projects.
FPT partners with Oracle to deploy Oracle Financial Services Analytical Applications (OFSAA) for banks.
In November 2024 the two signed a memorandum of understanding covering six Asia-Pacific markets: Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam.
It extends OFSAA work with Vietnamese banks since 2021 and widens Oracle’s regional delivery reach.
